fit: verified original exposure or clinical scope
assessment: The study contrasts isolated curcumin in α-synuclein protein states and assays cell viability. It reports different binding by protein state and reduced cell toxicity under selected comparisons. These molecular and cellular endpoints do not measure falls. The ingredient is a turmeric constituent. The full paper gives no ground turmeric or clinical Parkinson comparison. ACS lists December 3, 2012. PubMed indexes December 17, 2012 as electronic publication.

fit: verified original exposure or clinical scope
assessment: The main case-control model includes 486 Parkinson cases and 636 controls. Table 1 gives adjusted odds ratios per additional daily intake frequency of 0.83 (95% CI 0.56–1.24) for tomatoes and 0.77 (95% CI 0.41–1.44) for tomato juice. The questionnaire captures habitual intake categories, not isolated cooked tomato, and the dependent variable is Parkinson diagnosis rather than rigidity severity. The analysis mentions absent sauce and salsa data. The prior cucurbit reply uses the same cohort.

fit: isolated lycopene in mouse motor tasks
assessment: Five per group were assessed in open-field, pole, suspension and rotarod tasks. The isolated lycopene comparison improved pole timing and movement, with longer rotarod latency reported. The tasks and formulation do not measure cooked tomato effects on rigidity.
